scope: Primary source, instrument and metrological-method review for independent preparation and measurement feasibility.
checksum_scope: Hashes associate the actually retrieved source bytes only. They do not authenticate the publisher, scientific claims, future source availability or calibration provenance.
cache_scope: Optional ignored local source cache. The receipt contains no source PDF, measurement array or reserved response; cached bytes are not a repository or test dependency.
review_scope: Section references identify the reviewed method and specification claims. Paper figures were not extracted or selected as TNFR data. Downloaded source bytes are separate from web text review.

sources.title: Babenko et al. (2020), Characterization of a Josephson Junction Comb Generator
reviewed_sections: Printed p. 938, chip layout and measurement procedure
sources.factual_paraphrase: The RCSJ model supplies sinusoidal junction current and the voltage-phase row. The reported apparatus uses 1500 junctions, a 4 K chip and 5 GHz drive with separately calibrated measurements. The authors discuss nonsinusoidal behavior and junction variation as model discrepancies.
sources.scope_limit: This apparatus does not supply the C5 component matrices, the TNFR acquisition history, preparation bounds or frozen error allowances.

sources.title: English et al. (2016), Observation of non-sinusoidal current-phase relation in graphene Josephson junctions, arXiv:1305.0327v2
reviewed_sections: PDF p. 2, equations (1)-(2) and nonhysteretic inference condition
sources.factual_paraphrase: Phase-sensitive current-profile measurement uses a superconducting loop, flux transformer and DC SQUID. The refrigerator base temperature is 10 mK. The approximately 2 nH loop requires junction critical current below 135 nA for the stated nonhysteretic extraction regime.
sources.scope_limit: The loop and transfer model do not certify noninvasive initialization or the TNFR constituent phase and formation bounds.

sources.title: Andeen-Hagerling AH2700A capacitance bridge product brochure
reviewed_sections: PDF p. 2, averaging, zero correction and cable correction
sources.factual_paraphrase: The selected 1 kHz specifications list capacitance accuracy of plus or minus 5 ppm, stability below 1 ppm/year and temperature coefficient of plus or minus 0.035 ppm per degree Celsius. The brochure describes traceable calibration, fixture corrections and a speed-resolution tradeoff.
sources.scope_limit: The published headline accuracy alone does not certify the frozen 0.01 ppm scalar box. Specialized calibration is not excluded, and calibration of the full cryogenic matrix remains separate.

sources.title: NIST, Farad and Impedance Metrology
reviewed_sections: Major Accomplishments, digital four-arm bridge comparison
sources.factual_paraphrase: NIST reports a combined standard uncertainty of 5 parts per billion for a specialized comparison of a 100 kilohm resistor with a 1 nanofarad capacitor near 1592 Hz.
sources.scope_limit: This prevents a universal claim that 1e-8 calibration is unattainable; it does not establish deterministic calibration of this complete assembly over its operating history.

sources.title: JCGM 100:2008, Evaluation of measurement data - Guide to the expression of uncertainty in measurement
sources.factual_paraphrase: Expanded uncertainty concerns an interval with coverage supported by distributional assumptions. Reporting multiple output estimates includes covariance information.
sources.scope_limit: A confidence interval or RMS noise specification is not automatically a deterministic simultaneous bound for all 150 readings.

sources.title: NIST Special Publication 330, Section 2: The International System of Units
reviewed_sections: Section 2.2, definition of the SI and Table 1
sources.factual_paraphrase: The SI fixes h=6.62607015e-34 joule seconds and e=1.602176634e-19 coulombs exactly. Definition and practical realization are distinct.
sources.scope_limit: These supplied physical constants support the reference value a0=h/(4*pi*e), not a derivation of h or e from TNFR or an exact apparatus calibration.

sources.title: Tektronix / Keithley Model 2182A Nanovoltmeter product page
reviewed_sections: Features and benefits, low noise and two-channel measurement
sources.factual_paraphrase: The page describes two channels, 1 nV sensitivity and typical peak-to-peak noise of 15 nV at a 1 second response time, or 40 to 50 nV at 60 milliseconds.
sources.scope_limit: Typical noise is magnitude context, not a deterministic lower bound. Response time does not by itself specify the inward positive averaging kernel required by the frozen protocol.
